# changelog

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 — https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/ ; Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 — https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: entries are written from the project's own commit history and release diff, read directly from the repo; no other skill's output is an input. It feeds readme-writing and handover.
- **Feeds into:** readme-writing (README links the changelog), handover

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a project ships anything a user can notice — a release, a deprecation, a fix — and its CHANGELOG.md must be created, updated, or cut for release.
- **Do NOT use when:** recording internal work with no user effect (that belongs in the work log or commit history), or announcing a release socially (release notes and posts are written from the changelog, not instead of it). Do not keep a second change history in GitHub Releases that can drift from CHANGELOG.md (PM-124).

## Rules

1. **PM-121 — One file, newest first.** Exactly one CHANGELOG.md at the project root. `## [Unreleased]` sits on top; released sections follow in strictly descending version order. No per-year, per-component, or per-team changelog files.
2. **PM-122 — Entries land with the change.** Every user-visible change adds its entry to Unreleased in the same change (same PR/commit) as the behavior it describes. A release is never assembled by reconstructing entries from memory at release time.
3. **PM-123 — Six categories only.** Category headings are exactly: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security. No invented categories ("Misc", "Improvements", "Updates"), and an empty category is omitted, not left as a bare heading.
4. **PM-124 — One canonical history.** CHANGELOG.md is the single source of truth for change history. Release-page or store notes are generated or copied from it at release time, never maintained as a separate, editable copy.
5. **PM-125 — Written for users.** Each entry describes the effect on the user in one plain sentence: what they can now do, what behaves differently, what they must act on. Implementation details, internal codenames, and ticket IDs never appear.
6. **PM-126 — Curated, never generated.** Entries are selected and written by a human judgment pass. Merge commits and internal refactors with no user effect are omitted; one user-visible change is one entry, however many commits it took.
7. **PM-127 — The bump matches the content.** SemVer: breaking change → major, new feature → minor, fix only → patch. A release containing Removed entries or breaking Changed entries cannot ship as minor or patch; a release with Added entries is at least minor.
8. **PM-128 — Exact heading and date format.** Release headings are `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` with a real SemVer version and the actual release date in ISO 8601. Version labels are written the same way everywhere: no mixing of `v1.2`, `1.2`, and `Version 1.2.0`.
9. **PM-129 — No heading without a release.** A version section is created only when that version actually ships — a tag or published artifact exists for it. Planned versions live in Unreleased or the roadmap, never as empty or speculative version headings.
10. **PM-130 — The version source of truth is declared, never assumed.** The project states its version source — git tag, `package.json`, a `VERSION` file, or another stack-specific file — in the changelog header or project config. Gates read the version from that declared source only; no gate hardcodes a source.
11. **PM-131 — Every entry traces to a real change.** Each entry corresponds to a change actually merged in the release it sits under. An entry for work that was planned, reverted, or shipped in a different release is removed or moved, never left in place.
12. **PM-132 — Published sections are frozen.** After a version ships, its section is not silently edited. A factual error is corrected with a dated erratum note appended to that section, so the record shows both what was claimed and what was corrected.
13. **PM-133 — Deprecation precedes removal.** A feature appears under Deprecated at least one release before it appears under Removed, and the deprecation entry names the release in which removal is planned when that is known.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-061 — The dumped git log.** Banned: pasting raw commit output, merge commits, or commit hashes into CHANGELOG.md as entries. Defeats: DET-CON-004. Instead: curate the release into user-effect entries under the six categories (PM-125, PM-126) — the export fix becomes one Fixed entry, the merge and revert noise is omitted. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-062 — Entries for changes that never shipped.** Banned: changelog entries describing features, fixes, or behavior that are not in the release — planned, reverted, or imagined. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: the entry is deleted before release; if the feature ships later, its entry lands with that release (PM-131). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-063 — The content-free entry.** Banned: entries that carry no information about what changed — "bug fixes and improvements", "various enhancements", "performance improvements" with no behavior named. Defeats: DET-CON-006. Instead: name the user-visible effect: "Fixed: invoice PDFs no longer render a blank second page for multi-currency accounts." Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PM-064 — The phantom version heading.** Banned: a `## [X.Y.Z]` section for a version that was never tagged or published. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: unreleased work stays under `## [Unreleased]` until the version actually ships (PM-129). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-065 — Mixed version labels.** Banned: referring to versions inconsistently across the changelog and release surfaces — `v1.2`, `1.2`, `Version 1.2.0`, `Release 12` for the same versioning scheme. Defeats: DET-CON-017. Instead: one label form everywhere — the SemVer number in brackets in the changelog, matching the declared source of truth (PM-128, PM-130). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PM-061 — Heading and category parser.** Verifies: PM-121, PM-123, PM-128. Check: automated — a script asserts every `## ` heading in CHANGELOG.md matches `^## \[Unreleased\]$` or `^## \[(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\] - \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, the captured date parses as a real calendar date, and every `### ` heading is one of Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security. Pass: zero non-matching headings. Fail: block the release; fix the heading or category. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-062 — Order and date sequence.** Verifies: PM-121, PM-127. Check: automated — the parser from G-PM-061 additionally asserts version headings are in strictly descending SemVer order and their dates are non-increasing down the file. Pass: no inversions. Fail: block; reorder the sections — never edit a date to make the order pass. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-063 — Version source-of-truth match.** Verifies: PM-129, PM-130. Check: automated — read the project's declared version source (per PM-130: e.g. `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` stripped of a leading `v`, or the `version` field of `package.json`, or the contents of `VERSION`) and compare it with the topmost version heading in CHANGELOG.md. Pass: the two are exactly equal. Fail: block the release; either the release was not tagged or the heading is wrong — fix whichever is false. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-064 — Bump consistency.** Verifies: PM-127. Check: automated — diff the newest section's categories against the previous version: if Removed is present or any Changed entry is marked breaking, the major number must have increased; if Added is present, at least the minor number must have increased; a patch bump may contain only Fixed and Security entries. Pass: the actual bump is at least the required level. Fail: block; renumber the release before anything ships under the wrong version. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-065 — Entry-to-change cross-check.** Verifies: PM-122, PM-131. Check: manual, sampled — pick three entries from the newest release and trace each to a merged change (PR or commit) inside that release's range; separately, if the diff since the previous tag contains user-visible changes, Unreleased must not have been empty at release time. Pass: 3 of 3 entries trace to real changes. Fail: block; remove or move every untraceable entry and re-run. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Entries land with the change, not at release time.
- Written for users: effect, not implementation.
- Six categories, no inventions.
- No heading without a real release behind it.
- The bump must match the content — breaking means major.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every user-visible change in this release has an entry, added in the same change as the behavior (PM-122).
- [ ] All entries sit under the six categories only, one user effect per entry (PM-123, PM-125).
- [ ] No entry describes anything that is not actually in the release (PM-131, BAN-PM-062).
- [ ] Heading format, descending order, and ISO dates verified by G-PM-061 and G-PM-062.
- [ ] Top version heading equals the declared version source of truth (PM-130, G-PM-063).
- [ ] The version bump is consistent with the categories present (PM-127, G-PM-064).
- [ ] Deprecations were announced at least one release before any removal in this release (PM-133).
- [ ] Gates G-PM-061 to G-PM-065 pass; results recorded in progress.md.

# decision-logs

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Nygard, "Documenting Architecture Decisions" — https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions ; MADR 4.0.0 — https://adr.github.io/madr/ ; adr-tools — https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools
- **Depends on:** project-templates (emits `docs/adr/` and DECISIONS.md)
- **Feeds into:** progress-tracking, handover, memory-retrieval

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a project makes a significant, hard-to-reverse decision — stack, vendor, data model, protocol, a mandated-set change — or reverses one already recorded.
- **Do NOT use when:** the choice is trivially reversible or purely local (naming, formatting) — those belong in the work log or a commit message, not an ADR. Do not use DECISIONS.md as a second copy of the records; it is their index (PM-109).

## Rules

1. **PM-101 — One decision, one numbered file.** Each significant decision gets exactly one file in `docs/adr/`, named `NNNN-short-title.md`. Numbers are sequential and never reused; a withdrawn number stays withdrawn and is noted in DECISIONS.md.
2. **PM-102 — Written at decision time.** The record is created in the same change as the decision itself, while the context and the decider are known — never reconstructed later from chat or memory.
3. **PM-103 — Fixed structure.** Default to Nygard's five sections: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences. Escalate to MADR when the decision is contested, adding decision drivers, considered options with pros and cons, and a Confirmation section.
4. **PM-104 — Context is neutral fact.** Context states the forces, constraints, and evidence at play, without advocacy. Persuasion belongs in the options analysis and the Decision, never in Context.
5. **PM-105 — Decision in active voice, with a named decider.** The Decision reads "We will…" and the record names who decided (person or role) and the date. A record with no decider is incomplete.
6. **PM-106 — Consequences include the negatives.** Every record states what becomes harder, what is given up, and what risk is accepted — not only the benefits.
7. **PM-107 — Closed status lifecycle.** Status is exactly one of: proposed → accepted → deprecated, or superseded-by-ADR-NNNN. No other values, no free-text statuses.
8. **PM-108 — Accepted records are immutable except for Status.** A reversal is a new ADR that supersedes the old one and links to it; the old record's body is never edited, and its Status is updated to superseded-by-ADR-NNNN.
9. **PM-109 — DECISIONS.md is the index, not a copy.** The index lists each record's number, title, status, and link — and nothing else. Record content lives only in `docs/adr/`.
10. **PM-110 — Rejected options are recorded.** For contested decisions, each considered option is listed with why it lost. That record is what stops the decision being reopened later.
11. **PM-111 — Every fact in a record traces to evidence.** Figures, constraints, and claims in Context cite their source (a fact-sheet entry, a benchmark, a document). No number or constraint is invented to justify the choice.
12. **PM-112 — MADR records state how compliance is confirmed.** The Confirmation section names the check — a test, a review step, or a gate — that will show the decision is actually being followed.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-051 — Rewriting an accepted ADR in place.** Banned: editing the Context, Decision, or Consequences of an accepted record so the file no longer shows what was decided. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: leave ADR-0007 untouched, write ADR-0019 choosing Postgres, link it, and set ADR-0007's Status to superseded-by-ADR-0019. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-052 — Invented rationale.** Banned: stating figures, benchmarks, or constraints in Context that have no source behind them. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: cite the measurement or fact-sheet entry, or state the limit as an unverified assumption and mark it as one. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-053 — The non-decision.** Banned: a Decision section hedged until it commits to nothing. Defeats: DET-CON-009. Instead: "We will migrate the notification queue to SQS by 2026-12-01; the decider is the tech lead; revisit only if the cost ceiling in ADR-0011 is exceeded." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-054 — Index as second copy.** Banned: pasting full ADR text into DECISIONS.md alongside the record in `docs/adr/`. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: the index holds number, title, status, and link only (PM-109); readers follow the link to the single canonical record. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PM-055 — Reused or duplicated ADR number.** Banned: assigning a number that an earlier record already used, or two records sharing one number. Defeats: DET-CON-017. Instead: numbers are allocated once, in order, and never recycled; a withdrawn record keeps its number with Status deprecated. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PM-051 — Filename and numbering lint.** Verifies: PM-101. Check: automated — `ls docs/adr/ | grep -vE '^[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9-]+\.md$'` must print nothing, and `ls docs/adr/ | cut -d- -f1 | sort | uniq -d` must print nothing (no duplicate numbers). Pass: zero output from both commands. Fail: block the change; renumber before merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-052 — Index cross-check.** Verifies: PM-107, PM-109. Check: automated — script compares the set of files in `docs/adr/` against the links in DECISIONS.md and diffs each index status against the record's Status line. Pass: every record is indexed exactly once, every index link resolves, statuses agree. Fail: block; fix the index or the record, never both silently. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-053 — Status and section lint.** Verifies: PM-103, PM-107. Check: automated — for each record, `grep -E '^## Status' -A1` yields a value in {proposed, accepted, deprecated, superseded-by-ADR-NNNN}, and the five section headings Title/Status/Context/Decision/Consequences are all present. Pass: all records conform. Fail: block; correct the status value or add the missing section. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-054 — Immutability check.** Verifies: PM-108. Check: manual-assisted (script-supported) — for each accepted record, run the project's immutability script (sketch below) with the record's file and its acceptance commit. The script walks the `git log -p --follow` hunks after acceptance, tracks the current `## ` section from diff context lines, and prints a FLAG line for every added or removed line outside the Status section. The agent then reads each flagged line in the full diff and confirms it is a genuine body edit — hunk context can omit the section heading, so the script over-reports rather than under-reports, and the human/agent judgment on the flagged lines is part of the check. Pass: no confirmed body edits to any accepted record after its acceptance commit. Fail: block; restore the original body and express the change as a new superseding ADR. Recorded in: progress.md.

  ```bash
  # scripts/adr-immutability-check.sh FILE ACCEPTANCE_COMMIT
  git log -p --follow "$2..HEAD" -- "$1" | awk '
    /^diff --git/ { section = "" }
    /^ /  { if ($0 ~ /^ ## /) section = substr($0, 2); next }
    /^[+-]/ && $0 !~ /^\+\+\+/ && $0 !~ /^---/ {
      if (section != "## Status") print "FLAG: " $0
    }'
  ```

## Recall anchors

- One decision, one file, one number — never reused.
- Write it when you decide it, not when you remember it.
- Accepted means frozen; reversal means a new record.
- DECISIONS.md points; `docs/adr/` holds.
- Consequences include what it costs.

## Checklist

- [ ] Record created at decision time, in `docs/adr/`, with the next unused number (PM-101, PM-102).
- [ ] Five sections present; MADR escalation used if the decision was contested (PM-103).
- [ ] Decision is active voice and names the decider and date (PM-105).
- [ ] Negative consequences and rejected options are written down (PM-106, PM-110).
- [ ] Every fact in Context cites a source (PM-111).
- [ ] Status is a lifecycle value, and DECISIONS.md index entry added (PM-107, PM-109).
- [ ] Gates G-PM-051 to G-PM-054 pass; results recorded in progress.md.

# documentation-writing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Diátaxis — https://diataxis.fr/ ; Google developer documentation style guide, timeless documentation — https://developers.google.com/style/timeless-documentation ; Documentation checks in CI — https://datadef.io/guides/en/docs-checks-in-ci ; Documentation as code — https://sourcegraph.com/blog/documentation-as-code
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: docs are written from the product and code itself, checked against the running system; this skill sets the standards the other doc skills follow rather than consuming their output. It feeds readme-writing, runbook-writing, and changelog.
- **Feeds into:** readme-writing, runbook-writing, changelog

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** writing or revising any project documentation page — tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation — setting a project's doc standards, or reviewing docs before a release.
- **Do NOT use when:** the artifact is the README (use readme-writing), an incident procedure (runbook-writing), a decision record (decision-logs), a changelog (changelog), or marketing and site copy (D9 copywriting).

## Rules

1. **PM-021 — One page, one Diátaxis mode.** Every page is exactly one of tutorial (learning), how-to (task), reference (facts), or explanation (background), and the mode is declared in the page's front matter. A draft serving two modes is split before it ships.
2. **PM-022 — Verify before you write.** Every documented feature, flag, command, default value, and behavior is checked against the actual system — run it, or read the code/config that implements it — before the page ships. Behavior you cannot verify is not documented; it is filed as an open question.
3. **PM-023 — Name the reader need first.** Before drafting, state the reader and the job the page does for them in one line at the top of the draft. No identifiable reader need, no page.
4. **PM-024 — Docs as code.** Documentation lives in the same repository as the code it describes, in plain-text markup, reviewed in the same pull-request flow, and published on merge — never in a separate wiki or document store that drifts from the code.
5. **PM-025 — Docs ship with the code change.** A behavior change and its documentation change land in the same change. When that is impossible, a tracked doc-gap issue is filed in the same change and linked from the changed code or release notes.
6. **PM-026 — Owner and review trigger on every page.** Front matter carries `owner` and `last_reviewed`. A page is reviewed when code in its area changes or when its freshness window (a project-policy parameter) expires, whichever comes first.
7. **PM-027 — The word list governs terminology.** Product, feature, and concept names match the project word list and naming list exactly. A term not in the word list is defined at first use or not used.
8. **PM-028 — Write timelessly.** Document the current state in the present tense. "Currently", "new", "latest", and "now" never stand in for a version: version-specific facts carry the version number ("In 2.4, …") or are not stated.
9. **PM-029 — Match voice to mode.** How-tos address the reader in the imperative ("Run the migration"); tutorials guide step by step with the expected result at each step; reference pages state facts without narrative or persuasion.
10. **PM-030 — Execute every code sample.** Each command, API call, and config block in a page is run verbatim against the current system before the page ships or changes. A sample that fails is a documentation bug with the same priority as a code bug.
11. **PM-031 — One canonical page per fact.** A fact lives on exactly one page; other pages link to it instead of copying it. Duplicated passages found in review are replaced by links in the same change.
12. **PM-032 — Complete front matter or no merge.** Every page carries `mode`, `owner`, and `last_reviewed` in front matter. A page missing any field fails G-PM-011 and does not merge.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-011 — Documenting an unverified feature.** Banned: writing instructions, flags, or behaviors from a ticket, plan, or assumption without checking them against the running system. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: run the feature or read its implementation first (PM-022); document only what the system demonstrably does. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-012 — Scaffold and default text shipped as documentation.** Banned: publishing generator boilerplate, template prompts, or placeholder sections ("Add a description here", empty headed sections) as finished docs. Defeats: DET-CON-002. Instead: write the real content for the slot or delete the section; an honest gap is a tracked issue, not filler. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-013 — Draft markers in published docs.** Banned: `TODO`, `FIXME`, "content to follow", or "coming soon" (undated) in any published page, heading, or metadata field. Defeats: DET-CON-004. Instead: keep markers in the repo's issue tracker; published pages contain only finished statements. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PM-014 — Time-anchored claims left to rot.** Banned: "new for 2026", "our latest release", or undated "coming soon" feature claims on evergreen pages. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: state the fact with its version ("Dark mode, added in 1.8") and let the freshness gate (G-PM-014) retire stale claims. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PM-015 — Model-default register in docs.** Banned: dense AI filler vocabulary (delve, tapestry, realm, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's important to note") standing in for technical content. Defeats: DET-CON-007. Instead: cut to the subject; every paragraph names a component, mechanism, or fact the reader can check. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PM-011 — Structure and front-matter lint.** Verifies: PM-021, PM-026, PM-032. Check: automated — run `npx markdownlint-cli "docs/**/*.md"` and a front-matter script asserting every page has `mode`, `owner`, and `last_reviewed`; the same commands run locally as a script or in CI. Pass: exit 0 and zero pages missing a field. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-012 — Link check.** Verifies: PM-031. Check: automated — run `lychee docs/ README.md` for internal links on every change; external URLs on a scheduled run. Pass: zero broken internal links. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-013 — Style and terminology lint.** Verifies: PM-027, PM-028. Check: automated — run `vale --minAlertLevel=error docs/` with the project's word list and timeless-writing rules (flagging "currently/latest/new" as version substitutes) configured as the Vale style. Pass: zero error-level alerts. Fail: block merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-014 — Freshness gate.** Verifies: PM-026. Check: automated — a script reads `last_reviewed` from every page's front matter and fails any page older than the project's review window (policy parameter, set per project tier). Pass: no page past its window. Fail: block release until the page is reviewed and re-dated or the window is changed by a recorded decision. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-015 — Reader task test.** Verifies: PM-022, PM-023, PM-030. Check: manual — a reader unfamiliar with the material completes one learn, one task, and one lookup using only the docs, with no outside help. Pass: all three tasks completed; every stall is filed as a documentation bug. Fail: rework the failing pages and retest before the docs ship. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One page, one Diátaxis mode, one reader need.
- If you did not run it, do not document it.
- Docs ship with the code change — or the gap is a tracked issue.
- No "new", "latest", "currently": state the version or the fact.
- Every page: mode, owner, last_reviewed — or it does not merge.

## Checklist

- [ ] The page declares exactly one Diátaxis mode in its front matter (PM-021).
- [ ] Every documented behavior was verified against the actual system (PM-022).
- [ ] Owner and last_reviewed are set, and the review trigger is known (PM-026).
- [ ] All terms match the project word list; any new term is defined at first use (PM-027).
- [ ] No time-anchored word stands in for a version number (PM-028).
- [ ] Every code sample was executed verbatim and passed (PM-030).
- [ ] markdownlint, lychee, and Vale error-level checks pass locally (G-PM-011, G-PM-012, G-PM-013).
- [ ] The doc change ships with its code change, or a doc-gap issue is filed and linked (PM-025).

# handover

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Google Cloud Blog, "How SREs find the landmines in a service" (Production Readiness Review practice) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gcp/how-sres-find-the-landmines-in-a-service-cre-life-lessons ; datadef.io, docs checks in CI (freshness-gate pattern) — https://datadef.io/guides/en/docs-checks-in-ci ; Sourcegraph, "Documentation as code" — https://sourcegraph.com/blog/documentation-as-code
- **Depends on:** project-templates, progress-tracking, memory-retrieval
- **Feeds into:** none — handover is the terminal transfer step; its outputs are consumed by the receiving owner, not by another skill

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a project changes hands — new owner, new maintainer, end of engagement, or the single agent's work is picked up by a different operator. handover.md is maintained during the project and finalized at transfer; this skill runs the readiness review and the acceptance test that close the transfer.
- **Do NOT use when:** recording day-to-day status (progress-tracking), writing the runbooks and postmortems that transfer (runbook-writing, postmortem-writing), or recording why decisions were made (decision-logs). This skill verifies and transfers the project's memory; it does not author it.

## Rules

1. **PM-181 — Handover is a process, not a document.** It runs as a readiness review against a checklist — mandated file set fresh and complete, architecture and failure-mode walkthroughs, landmines list, credentials path, acceptance — modeled on Google's Production Readiness Review. A file drop with no review is not a handover.
2. **PM-182 — No handover without a named accepting owner.** The receiver is a named person or role who agrees to take the project on. A transfer addressed to "the team" or to nobody has not happened.
3. **PM-183 — Acceptance is recorded, with a date.** handover.md records who accepted, in what role, on which ISO 8601 date, and what scope they accepted. Undated or unsigned acceptance does not count.
4. **PM-184 — Landmines are listed explicitly, each with evidence.** Every open risk, known fragility, and unresolved follow-up appears in the landmines list with evidence or a link to where the evidence lives. If there are none, handover.md states "no known landmines" as a finding — silence is never read as none.
5. **PM-185 — Credentials path, never credentials.** Handover materials name each system, where its secrets live (vault, provider, owner), and the procedure by which access is granted or transferred. Secret values — passwords, tokens, keys — never appear in handover.md or any transferred document.
6. **PM-186 — The memory transfers, not only the code.** Runbooks, postmortems, DECISIONS.md and the ADR set, progress.md, and the fact sheet are line items in the transfer manifest. A receiver who gets code without the project's memory has received a partial handover.
7. **PM-187 — Failure modes are walked through, not just listed.** Before sign-off, the giver walks the receiver through the architecture and the known failure modes — what breaks, how it presents, which runbook answers it. The walkthrough is recorded in handover.md with its date and participants.
8. **PM-188 — The mandated set is fresh at transfer.** Every mandated file is present and within its freshness window (a project-policy parameter, per file tier) at the transfer date. A stale runbook or a kickoff-era progress.md is refreshed or flagged as a gap before sign-off, not discovered after.
9. **PM-189 — Open work transfers with owners.** Every blocked item, postmortem follow-up, and deferred fix open at transfer is listed with its current owner, its state, and what unblocks or completes it, so nothing open depends on the giver's memory after they leave.
10. **PM-190 — The cold run is the acceptance test.** Using only the handover materials, the receiving owner deploys the project, finds the runbook for a named incident class, names the top open risks, and states who accepted the transfer and when. Any failed step is a handover gap.
11. **PM-191 — Gaps block sign-off and are recorded.** A failed cold-run step, a missing mandated file, or an unlisted landmine is written into handover.md as a gap with an owner and a fix date. Sign-off waits until gaps are closed or the accepting owner explicitly accepts them in writing in handover.md.
12. **PM-192 — handover.md is maintained during the project.** It is updated as owners, risks, and systems change, and finalized at transfer. A handover.md authored from scratch on the exit day is a defect — it will carry the author's memory gaps as the project's record.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-091 — Secret values in handover materials.** Banned: pasting passwords, API keys, tokens, or recovery codes into handover.md, a transferred doc, or the transfer message. Defeats: DET-CON-003. Instead: name the system, the vault or provider where the secret lives, and the grant procedure — the receiver is given access through that procedure, never the value in a document. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-092 — The link-and-cheer handover.** Banned: a transfer consisting of a repository link and an encouraging message, with no review, no walkthrough, and no acceptance. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: run the readiness review (PM-181), walk the failure modes (PM-187), and close with a recorded, dated acceptance (PM-183). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-093 — Landmines by omission.** Banned: a handover whose risks section is empty, absent, or "all good" while the project's own records — progress.md blockers, postmortem follow-ups, the issue tracker — name open risks. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: build the landmines list from the project's records, each entry with evidence or a link; "none known" appears only as an explicit finding after that check. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-094 — The code-only transfer.** Banned: transferring the repository without the project memory — runbooks, postmortems, DECISIONS.md/ADRs, progress.md — while handover.md claims a complete transfer. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: the memory set is a line item in the transfer manifest (PM-186) and the manifest gate (G-PM-091) fails until each item is present in the transferred repo. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-095 — The exit-day handover.** Banned: a handover.md written entirely at exit, presenting kickoff-era or from-memory content as the project's current state. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: maintain handover.md during the project (PM-192); at transfer, re-verify each section against the current repo and records, and date the verification. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PM-091 — Mandated-file manifest and freshness check.** Verifies: PM-186, PM-188. Check: automated — a script diffs the repo's file list against the mandated set for the project type (the project-templates manifest) and asserts every memory-set item (runbooks, postmortems, DECISIONS.md, docs/adr/, progress.md, fact sheet, handover.md) is present; then for each file carrying a `last_reviewed` date or git-tracked mtime, asserts it falls within its freshness window (project-policy parameter). Pass: zero mandated files missing, zero outside their window unflagged. Fail: each miss or stale file is recorded as a handover gap (PM-191); sign-off is blocked. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-092 — Secrets scan and credentials-path check.** Verifies: PM-185. Check: automated — grep the handover materials and transfer manifest for credential patterns (high-entropy strings, `password`, `secret`, `token`, `api_key` followed by a value, private-key headers); assert zero matches, and assert handover.md has a credentials-path section naming at least one system with its secret location and grant procedure. Pass: zero secret-value matches and the path section present. Fail: remove the value, rotate the exposed secret, and re-run; sign-off is blocked until clean. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-093 — Acceptance record check.** Verifies: PM-182, PM-183. Check: automated — grep handover.md for the acceptance block: a named accepting owner (person or role), an ISO 8601 date, and the accepted scope. Pass: all three present and the date is the transfer date or later. Fail: no acceptance, no handover — the transfer stays open in progress.md. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-094 — Landmines cross-check.** Verifies: PM-184, PM-189. Check: automated assist — extract open items from progress.md (blocked entries), postmortem follow-up actions not marked closed, and any open risks in the issue tracker export; diff against the landmines list in handover.md. Pass: every open item appears in the landmines list with evidence or a link, or is explicitly closed with a date. Fail: add the missing entries and re-run; an unexplained diff blocks sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-095 — Cold-run acceptance test.** Verifies: PM-187, PM-190. Check: manual — the receiving owner, using only the handover materials and no help from the giver: (1) deploys or starts the project following the transferred docs, (2) finds the runbook for a named incident class, (3) names the top open risks from the landmines list, (4) states who accepted the transfer and on what date. Pass: 4 of 4 steps completed unaided. Fail: each failed step is recorded as a gap with an owner and fix date (PM-191); the cold run repeats after fixes before sign-off. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- No named accepting owner, no handover.
- Acceptance is recorded, dated, and scoped — or it did not happen.
- Landmines are listed with evidence; silence never means none.
- Credentials path, never credentials.
- The memory transfers with the code — and the cold run proves it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Readiness review run against the mandated set; manifest and freshness gate passes (G-PM-091).
- [ ] Landmines list built from the project's records, each entry with evidence or a link (PM-184, G-PM-094).
- [ ] Credentials path names every system, secret location, and grant procedure — and the secrets scan is clean (PM-185, G-PM-092).
- [ ] Failure-mode walkthrough held and recorded with date and participants (PM-187).
- [ ] Runbooks, postmortems, DECISIONS.md/ADRs, and progress.md are in the transfer manifest (PM-186).
- [ ] Cold run passed 4 of 4, or every failed step is recorded as a gap with an owner and fix date (G-PM-095, PM-191).
- [ ] Acceptance block present in handover.md: named owner, ISO date, accepted scope (PM-183, G-PM-093).

# memory-retrieval

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Docs as code (Sourcegraph) — https://sourcegraph.com/blog/documentation-as-code ; GitHub Docs, creating a default community health file — https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file
- **Depends on:** project-templates, readme-writing, decision-logs
- **Feeds into:** handover, progress-tracking

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** designing or auditing how a project's own record is found again — canonical locations for facts, index pages, file and heading naming, superseded-document handling, and the tests that prove a fresh reader (or the single agent returning later) can retrieve what the project knows using only the repo.
- **Do NOT use when:** the task is writing the documents themselves (documentation-writing, readme-writing, runbook-writing own content), recording a decision (decision-logs), or transferring the project (handover — this skill supplies handover's retrieval acceptance tests, not the transfer process).

## Rules

1. **PM-161 — One canonical home per fact.** Every fact (version, database choice, price, escalation path, status) is stated in exactly one file. Every other document that needs it links to that file; it never restates the value.
2. **PM-162 — Fixed names and locations.** Mandated files use the set's fixed names and paths. A project never renames, moves, or re-extensions a mandated file to suit local taste.
3. **PM-163 — Two hops maximum.** Every mandated file is reachable from README.md or the docs index in at most two link hops. A file no index path reaches is treated as missing.
4. **PM-164 — Indexes link, never restate.** DECISIONS.md links every ADR; the README and docs index link every mandated file. An index entry is a title plus a link — copying the target's content into the index creates a second home and violates PM-161.
5. **PM-165 — Duplicates become links on sight.** When a duplicated fact is noticed, the non-canonical copy is replaced by a link to the canonical home in the same change — not filed for later cleanup.
6. **PM-166 — Superseded means marked, never silently deleted.** A replaced document stays in place with a SUPERSEDED banner naming and linking its replacement. Deleting or overwriting it without the marker is forbidden, so an old answer is always visibly old.
7. **PM-167 — Guessable terms.** File names, headings, and vocabulary follow the set's conventions and the project word list, so a searcher can guess the term that will hit (decision → DECISIONS.md and `docs/adr/`, incident → postmortem and runbook). One concept, one term, everywhere.
8. **PM-168 — Repo-only retrieval.** Retrieval must work with the repo alone: plain-text search (`grep`, `git log`) over consistently named files, plus the index pages. No hosted search service, wiki, or chat history may be a required step in finding a project fact.
9. **PM-169 — The project owns a query list.** Every project maintains `retrieval-queries.md`: at least 10 known-fact questions a newcomer would actually ask (which database, current version, on-call escalation, how to deploy), each naming the canonical file that answers it. It is created at project start and extended whenever a new class of fact appears.
10. **PM-170 — Test with the project's own questions.** The scripted known-fact search runs PM-169's list, never a generic list shipped with a template — a generic list tests the template's facts, not the project's.
11. **PM-171 — Crawl on cadence.** The orphan crawl (G-PM-081) and the known-fact search (G-PM-082) run at every release or work-cycle boundary, and their results are recorded in progress.md like any other gate.
12. **PM-172 — Change the home, then sweep.** When a fact changes, only its canonical home is edited; before the change closes, a repo-wide search for the old value returns no live copies (hits inside marked superseded documents and the changelog are the only permitted remains).

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-081 — The copied fact.** Banned: pasting a fact's value into a second document instead of linking to its canonical home. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: state the fact once in its canonical home and link to it from every other document (PM-161). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-082 — The vanished predecessor.** Banned: deleting or silently overwriting a superseded document so no trace of the replacement relationship remains. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: keep the document, add a SUPERSEDED banner, and link to its replacement (PM-166). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-083 — The renamed mandated file.** Banned: giving a mandated file a project-specific name or location (`our-decisions.md`, `docs/final/ARCHITECTURE-v2.md`). Defeats: DET-CON-017. Instead: use the set's fixed name and path; put project flavor in the content, not the filename (PM-162). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PM-084 — The mirrored document.** Banned: copying a whole document into additional folders "for convenience" (the runbook duplicated under docs/, ops/, and the service folder). Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: keep one canonical document and link to it from each place that needs it (PM-161, PM-165). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PM-081 — Orphan crawl.** Verifies: PM-163, PM-164. Check: automated — starting at README.md and the docs index, follow Markdown links to depth 2 and diff the reached set against the mandated file manifest: `grep -rhoE '\]\([^)]+\.md\)' README.md docs/ | sort -u`, compared with the manifest list. Pass: every mandated file is reached; zero orphans. Fail: block shipment until the file is linked or the manifest is corrected. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-082 — Known-fact search test.** Verifies: PM-169, PM-170. Check: automated — for each row of `retrieval-queries.md`, run `grep -ril '<query term>' --include='*.md' .` and confirm the row's named canonical file appears among the hits. Pass: 10 of 10 queries return their canonical file. Fail: fix naming, headings, or the canonical home — never edit the query list to match a broken layout. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-083 — Duplicate-value sweep.** Verifies: PM-161, PM-172. Check: automated — sample five load-bearing facts from their canonical homes (current version, database, escalation path, deploy command, support promise) and `grep -rn '<value>' --include='*.md' .`; each value must appear definitionally in exactly one file, elsewhere only inside links, the changelog, or marked superseded documents. Pass: no live second home for any sampled fact. Fail: replace the copies with links (PM-165) and re-run. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-084 — Superseded-marker check.** Verifies: PM-166. Check: automated — every file the index or DECISIONS.md marks superseded carries a SUPERSEDED banner linking its replacement: `grep -L 'SUPERSEDED' <superseded files>` returns nothing; `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only` shows no mandated document deleted without a superseding entry. Pass: both checks clean. Fail: restore and mark the document before shipping. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-085 — Fresh-reader retrieval test.** Verifies: PM-167, PM-168. Check: manual — a reader or agent with no prior project context answers five questions drawn from `retrieval-queries.md` using only the repo (no asking the author, no chat history), timed. Pass: all five answered correctly from canonical files within the project's agreed time budget. Fail: each miss is a retrieval defect — fix the index, name, or canonical home, then retest. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- One fact, one home; everything else is a link.
- If it is not reachable in two hops, it does not exist.
- Mark superseded — never silently delete.
- Test retrieval with the project's own questions.
- If grep cannot find it, the project does not know it.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every sampled fact has exactly one canonical home; all other mentions are links (PM-161, G-PM-083).
- [ ] All mandated files use the set's fixed names and paths (PM-162).
- [ ] Orphan crawl passes: zero mandated files unreachable within two hops (G-PM-081).
- [ ] `retrieval-queries.md` exists with ≥10 project questions, each naming its canonical file (PM-169).
- [ ] Known-fact search test passes 10/10 against the project's own list (G-PM-082).
- [ ] Every superseded document carries a SUPERSEDED banner linking its replacement (PM-166, G-PM-084).
- [ ] Fresh-reader test passed and recorded in progress.md (G-PM-085).

# postmortem-writing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** Google SRE Workbook, "Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure" — https://sre.google/workbook/postmortem-culture/ ; Atlassian, "Incident postmortems" — https://www.atlassian.com/incident-management/handbook/postmortems
- **Depends on:** runbook-writing (the runbook used in the incident is an input and a link target), progress-tracking (incidents and postmortems are recorded there)
- **Feeds into:** progress-tracking, handover, runbook-writing (lessons learned update the runbook that failed)

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an incident meets one of the project's configured postmortem triggers (PM-081) — user-visible downtime, data loss, manual on-call intervention, or a severity at or above the project's mandatory threshold.
- **Do NOT use when:** the event was a routine deployment, a caught-in-testing defect, or a near-miss below every trigger — those get a work-log or runbook note, not a postmortem. Do not use it to assign personal blame; that is the failure this skill exists to prevent (BAN-PM-041).

## Rules

1. **PM-081 — Triggers are configured parameters, never hardcoded.** The project sets its own trigger thresholds — severity levels, downtime minutes, data-loss classes — in its project files before incidents happen. Google SRE's triggers (user-visible downtime, data loss, on-call manual intervention) and Atlassian's (severity 1–2 mandatory) are worked examples to start from, not universal values; a small project copies the shape and sets its own numbers.
2. **PM-082 — Blameless by construction.** People are referred to by role ("the on-call engineer", "the deployer"), never named as a cause. Every cause is framed as a system or process property: what the system allowed, lacked, or failed to signal.
3. **PM-083 — Fixed structure, all sections present.** Every postmortem carries, in order: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Contributing causes, Mitigation, Follow-up actions. A missing section is an incomplete postmortem, not a stylistic choice.
4. **PM-084 — The timeline is built from records, never memory.** Each timeline entry carries a timestamp and its source (alert log, deploy log, monitoring graph, chat log). An event whose time cannot be sourced is marked "time unverified" — it is never given a plausible-looking time.
5. **PM-085 — Impact is measured, not estimated.** Duration, scope (users, requests, data affected), and severity come from monitoring and incident records. A figure with no record behind it is stated as unknown, not rounded into existence.
6. **PM-086 — Causes are contributing and multiple.** The analysis names every contributing system/process factor, plural. A single "root cause" line that stops at the triggering event — and any analysis that ends at "human error" — is incomplete: the question is always what made that action possible and its effect undetected.
7. **PM-087 — Every follow-up action has an owner, a due date, and a tracking ID.** Owner is a named person or role, the due date is an ISO date, and the tracking ID points at the project's tracker. An action missing any of the three does not count as an action and blocks closure.
8. **PM-088 — A named owner drives it to closure.** One named postmortem owner (by role) drives drafting, review, and approval. The postmortem closes only when every preventive action is filed in the tracker and tracked — writing the document is not closure.
9. **PM-089 — Review includes a blameless-language pass by a non-participant.** Someone not involved in the incident reviews the draft specifically for blame framing, memory-sourced timeline entries, and unsupported figures, before the postmortem is published.
10. **PM-090 — Published where the team can find it, and linked.** The finished postmortem lives in the project's postmortem location (repo or docs index) and is linked from progress.md and from the runbook for that incident class.
11. **PM-091 — Corrections are appended, never silently rewritten.** If a fact in a published postmortem turns out wrong, a dated correction note is appended stating what changed and why. The original text is not edited to look as if it was always right.
12. **PM-092 — Lessons reach the runbook.** Any procedure gap the incident exposed is fixed in the relevant runbook in the same change that closes the postmortem, or filed as a follow-up action under PM-087.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-041 — Naming a person as the cause.** Banned: any sentence that makes an individual the cause of the incident ("the outage happened because Alex deployed without checking"). Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: "Contributing cause: the admin console listed two services under the same display name and the restart action required no confirmation; the on-call engineer (role) selected the staging entry." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-042 — Timeline from memory.** Banned: timeline entries with timestamps reconstructed from recollection or rounded to plausible times, with no log source. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: every entry cites its source — "13:47 — alert fired (alert log #A-2214); 14:31 — rollback initiated (deploy log)". Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-043 — "Be more careful" actions.** Banned: follow-up actions that are exhortations or intentions — "be more careful", "double-check next time", "pay more attention" — or any action with no owner, due date, or tracking ID. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: "Action: add a pre-migration dry-run check to the deploy pipeline. Owner: platform lead. Due: 2026-12-05. Tracker: OPS-118." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-044 — Invented impact figures.** Banned: impact numbers with no monitoring or incident record behind them ("about 10,000 users were affected", "roughly two hours of downtime") presented as findings. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: "Impact: 41 minutes of elevated errors (monitoring, incident window 13:47–14:28); affected-user count not measured — recorded as unknown." Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-045 — The single root cause that stops at the trigger.** Banned: a Contributing causes section with one line naming the triggering event or a person's action as "the root cause", with no system or process factors. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: list each contributing factor: the field was unvalidated, staging did not mirror the production value, and the deploy had no canary stage. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PM-041 — Section completeness check.** Verifies: PM-083. Check: automated — `grep -cE '^## (Summary|Impact|Timeline|Contributing causes|Mitigation|Follow-up actions)' postmortem-<incident>.md` returns 6. Pass: all six sections present. Fail: block publication; add the missing section. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-042 — Action-row completeness check.** Verifies: PM-087. Check: automated — parse the Follow-up actions table and assert every row has non-empty Action, Owner, Due date (matching `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`), and Tracking ID fields, e.g. `awk -F'|' 'NR>2 && NF>5 && ($3=="" || $4=="" || $5=="" || $6=="") {print "incomplete action row:", NR}' postmortem-<incident>.md` prints nothing. Pass: zero incomplete rows. Fail: block closure until each action is owned, dated, and tracked. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-043 — Blame and vagueness lint.** Verifies: PM-082, PM-086, PM-087. Check: automated plus manual — `grep -inE 'be more careful|double-check next time|pay more attention|root cause: (a |the )?(human|operator|engineer)' postmortem-<incident>.md` prints nothing, and the PM-089 non-participant reviewer signs off that no person is named as a cause. Pass: no lint hits and reviewer sign-off recorded. Fail: rewrite the flagged passages as system/process causes before publication. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-044 — Timeline sourcing and linkage check.** Verifies: PM-084, PM-090. Check: automated — every Timeline row carries a source marker (log, alert, or record reference) or the words "time unverified", and `grep -l 'postmortem-<incident>' progress.md <runbook>.md` lists both files. Pass: all entries sourced or marked, both links present. Fail: block publication; source the entries from the logs and add the links. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Blame the system that allowed it, never the person who did it.
- Timeline from logs, or mark it unverified — never from memory.
- Causes are plural; "human error" is where analysis starts, not ends.
- No owner, no due date, no tracking ID — no action.
- Closed means the preventive actions are tracked, not that the document is written.

## Checklist

- [ ] Incident met a configured trigger, and the trigger values came from the project's own settings (PM-081).
- [ ] All six sections present: Summary, Impact, Timeline, Contributing causes, Mitigation, Follow-up actions (PM-083).
- [ ] People appear by role only; every cause is a system or process property (PM-082).
- [ ] Every timeline entry is timestamped with its log source, or marked "time unverified" (PM-084).
- [ ] Impact figures come from monitoring/incident records; unmeasured values are stated as unknown (PM-085).
- [ ] Every follow-up action has an owner, an ISO due date, and a tracking ID (PM-087).
- [ ] Non-participant blameless review passed, postmortem published and linked from progress.md and the runbook (PM-089, PM-090).
- [ ] Gates G-PM-041 to G-PM-044 pass; results recorded in progress.md.

---

<!-- generated from skills/project-memory/progress-tracking/SKILL.md (bundle form) -->

# progress-tracking

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** datadef.io, docs checks in CI (freshness-gate pattern) — https://datadef.io/guides/en/docs-checks-in-ci ; Sourcegraph, "Documentation as code" — https://sourcegraph.com/blog/documentation-as-code
- **Depends on:** project-templates, decision-logs
- **Feeds into:** handover, memory-retrieval, postmortem-writing

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** any work starts, changes state, blocks, or finishes on a project — progress.md is updated as part of that work, and every gate result from every skill is recorded here. Anyone asking "where does this project stand?" is answered from this file.
- **Do NOT use when:** recording history or rationale — effort narration belongs in the work log and git, decisions belong in DECISIONS.md via decision-logs, incident analysis belongs in postmortem-writing. progress.md holds current verified state only.

## Rules

1. **PM-141 — One status of record.** progress.md is the project's single status file. Status maintained in chat, a dashboard, or a README section instead is merged into progress.md or deleted.
2. **PM-142 — Verified state only.** An item is marked done only when its gate result is recorded in progress.md. Attempted, drafted, or "should work" is in progress — never done.
3. **PM-143 — Gate results land here.** Every gate run, from every skill loaded for the work, records its result in progress.md: gate ID, pass or fail, date. A gate with no recorded result is treated as never run.
4. **PM-144 — Every entry is dated.** Each status entry carries an ISO 8601 date. An undated entry is treated as stale: re-verify it or remove it at the next update.
5. **PM-145 — Done names the artifact.** Every done item names or links what was produced. A done claim whose artifact cannot be found in the repo is not done.
6. **PM-146 — Updated with the work.** progress.md is updated in the same change as the work it reports. A separate status-update commit made later is a process defect.
7. **PM-147 — Blocked is a triple.** A blocked item names the blocker, the blocker's owner, and the condition that unblocks it. "Waiting" alone is not a status.
8. **PM-148 — Four states only.** Entries are done, in progress, blocked, or next. No other status vocabulary: "almost done", "wrapping up", and "90%" are not states.
9. **PM-149 — State, not effort.** progress.md reports state. Hours spent, difficulty, and history belong in the work log and git history, never in the status file.
10. **PM-150 — Decisions and incidents link out.** A decision made during the work is appended to DECISIONS.md via decision-logs and linked from progress.md; an incident links its postmortem. progress.md is never the only copy of either.
11. **PM-151 — Next is concrete.** The Next section names the upcoming actions, each with an owner. An empty Next while unfinished work exists is a defect.
12. **PM-152 — Stale entries are resolved, not carried.** At each update, entries older than the current work cycle are re-verified against the deliverable, then corrected or deleted — never silently carried forward.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-071 — Done on attempt.** Banned: marking an item done because the work was attempted or drafted, with no gate result recorded. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: run the gate, record its result with gate ID and date, and only then mark the item done. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-072 — The invented percentage.** Banned: progress figures ("80% complete", "frontend 90% done") with no counted list of items behind them. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: report counts over a named item list ("14 of 16 screens pass their gates"), or report states with no percentage. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-073 — The kickoff fossil.** Banned: progress.md entries that predate the current work cycle presented as current status. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: update the file in the same change as the work; re-verify or delete stale entries at every update. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-074 — Template status shipped.** Banned: generator boilerplate or placeholder text ("Project status — TODO", "coming soon") surviving in a shipped progress.md. Defeats: DET-CON-004. Instead: replace boilerplate with dated, verified entries at project start, or delete the placeholder line. Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-PM-075 — The bare "blocked".** Banned: a blocked entry naming no blocker, no owner, and no unblocking condition. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: record the triple — what blocks, who owns the blocker, what unblocks it — plus a re-check date. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PM-071 — Freshness gate.** Verifies: PM-144, PM-146. Check: automated — `git log -1 --format=%cs -- progress.md` must fall within the current work cycle (project policy window, default 7 days while work is active), and a grep confirms every entry line carries an ISO date. Pass: both conditions true. Fail: all status is treated as stale; update progress.md before any status report leaves the project. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-072 — Done-artifact check.** Verifies: PM-142, PM-145. Check: automated — extract the file paths and links named by done entries and assert each exists (`test -f` for paths, link resolution for URLs). Pass: every done item's artifact exists. Fail: the item reverts to in progress until the artifact exists. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-073 — Gate-result completeness.** Verifies: PM-143. Check: automated — collect the gate IDs recorded in progress.md and diff them against the gate IDs of the skills loaded for the current work. Pass: every loaded skill's gates appear with a pass/fail result and a date. Fail: block the status report; run the missing gates or record why they do not apply. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-074 — Sampled truth audit.** Verifies: PM-142, PM-152. Check: manual — sample three entries (one done, one in progress, one blocked) and confirm each against the actual deliverable, the named blocker owner, and the repo state. Pass: 3 of 3 match reality. Fail: correct the file and re-audit the full entry list. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Done means a gate result is recorded — not attempted, recorded.
- Every entry dated; undated is stale.
- Done names the artifact; no artifact, no done.
- Blocked is a triple: blocker, owner, unblocking condition.
- Update progress.md in the same change as the work.

## Checklist

- [ ] progress.md updated in the same change as the work it reports (PM-146).
- [ ] Every done item has its gate result recorded, with gate ID and date (PM-143).
- [ ] Every done item names or links an artifact that exists (G-PM-072).
- [ ] No undated entries; stale entries re-verified or removed (PM-144, PM-152).
- [ ] Every blocked item names blocker, owner, and unblocking condition (PM-147).
- [ ] No percentage appears without a counted item list behind it (BAN-PM-072).
- [ ] Decisions appended to DECISIONS.md and incidents linked to their postmortems (PM-150).

# project-templates

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/creating-a-template-repository ; https://simonwillison.net/2021/Aug/28/dynamic-github-repository-templates/ ; https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: this skill owns the scaffold itself; its input is the mandated project file set defined in this repo, not another skill's output — every project starts here. It feeds readme-writing, documentation-writing, progress-tracking, and handover.
- **Feeds into:** readme-writing, documentation-writing, progress-tracking, handover

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a new project repository is being created, the mandated file set changes, or the project template itself is being revised. This skill owns the scaffold every project starts from.
- **Do NOT use when:** the project already exists and only its content needs work (use the owning skill — readme-writing, changelog, decision-logs), or when backfilling one missing file by hand would leave the template unchanged (fix the template, then regenerate).

## Rules

1. **PM-001 — Full mandated set, or a recorded exception.** Generation emits the full extended mandated set for the project type (the Appendix A files plus the D-006 additions: LICENSE, CODEOWNERS, `docs/adr/`, issue and PR templates, .gitignore, dependabot.yml). Every file not emitted is listed in the generation record as not-applicable with a reason. A file is never silently absent.
2. **PM-002 — Templates carry variables, not content.** Template files contain structure, headings, fill-in prompts, and substitution tokens (`{{project_name}}`, `{{owner}}`, stack choices) — nothing else. A token is a variable to be replaced at generation time, never prose to be read.
3. **PM-003 — No invented facts, ever.** No template ships a name, metric, date, contact detail, testimonial, team member, or capability claim as sample content. Where a real project would state a fact, the template carries a prompt naming where the fact comes from (fact-sheet.md, the owner's input) — never a plausible invention.
4. **PM-004 — Empty sections stay honestly empty.** A section with no real content yet keeps its heading and its fill-in prompt, and nothing more. Filler prose written to make a section look finished is a defect, even when it is generic.
5. **PM-005 — Conditional files fire on triggers only.** CONTENT_METADATA, PAYMENT_SECURITY, and CLONE_DESIGN_SYSTEM are emitted only when the project type triggers them (content publishing, payments, a clone build). A condition stated in the owning playbook (for example, a step marked "if paid", or a recorded stack choice the file depends on) is a trigger for this rule: when the condition does not hold, the file is recorded not-applicable in the generation record with the condition as the reason. Where the owning playbook has not yet defined the trigger, the gap is recorded in the generation record — the drafter does not guess the classification.
6. **PM-006 — Generation is one reproducible command.** A fresh project is produced by running a generator (cookiecutter-style, Jinja + `cookiecutter.json`, or any equivalent) against the versioned template. Generation means producing exactly the file set listed in the project type's shipped manifest, `templates/mandated-manifest-<type>.txt` — the manifest is the normative artifact: where a generator's output and the manifest disagree, the manifest governs and the generator is fixed. GitHub template repositories copy structure but substitute no variables, so they are never the whole mechanism. Hand-assembling the file set is not generation. This repository ships a reference generator for exactly this contract — `python3 scripts/generate-project.py --type <type> --target <dir>` emits the manifest's file set (the template file where `templates/` carries one, an honest empty-section scaffold otherwise) and prints the manifest diff result; any equivalent generator satisfies the rule the same way.
7. **PM-007 — Output is never hand-patched.** A defect found in a generated project is fixed in the template and the project is regenerated, or the fix is recorded as a deliberate project-level divergence. Editing only the output guarantees the next project inherits the defect.
8. **PM-008 — The template is versioned and changelogged.** The template carries a semantic version and a changelog entry per change, like a product. A version with no changelog entry does not ship.
9. **PM-009 — Mandated-set changes are decisions first.** Any change that adds, removes, or renames a mandated file is recorded in the decision log before the template ships it. The template never drifts ahead of the recorded set.
10. **PM-010 — Public projects get the community files.** CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SUPPORT, and GOVERNANCE are emitted when the project is public, on top of GitHub's recognized community-profile floor (README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY). For a private project they are recorded not-applicable under PM-001, not forgotten. SECURITY in that floor is a single file with two named sections — vulnerability reporting (how to report) and the project's security design — never two separate files with the same name.
11. **PM-011 — Generated output passes the gates from the first commit.** A generated project passes markdownlint and the link checks with zero errors before its first commit. "We'll lint it later" is how unlinted scaffolds become permanent.
12. **PM-012 — Every template change is self-tested.** Before a template change merges, a sample project is regenerated from it and gates G-PM-001 to G-PM-003 are run against the output. An untested template change does not merge.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-001 — Invented social proof baked into the template.** Banned: template output containing sample testimonials, user counts, ratings, or press mentions presented as the project's own. Defeats: DET-CON-010. Instead: the README carries the heading and a prompt — "List real customers only, each with a producible source record (see real-content)" (PM-003). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-002 — Scaffold boilerplate shipped as project content.** Banned: generator or theme defaults surviving into the shipped files — a scaffold README describing the template itself, "Hello world!" posts, "Add a description here". Defeats: DET-CON-002. Instead: every default string is replaced by project structure and prompts at generation time, or the file is not emitted (PM-002). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-003 — Unreplaced substitution tokens in shipped files.** Banned: `{{project_name}}`, `{{owner}}`, or any `{{ }}` token visible in a committed project file. Defeats: DET-CON-003. Instead: generation fails unless every declared variable has a value, and gate G-PM-002 scans the output before the first commit. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-004 — Compliance furniture without the process.** Banned: emitting a conditional file that asserts a practice the project does not run — above all a PAYMENT_SECURITY.md describing controls that do not exist. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: conditional files fire only on their real trigger (PM-005) and describe only processes that exist. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-005 — Draft markers left in generated files.** Banned: TODO, FIXME, or "content to follow" strings in any generated file's fields, headings, or metadata. Defeats: DET-CON-004. Instead: an unknown value is an unfilled variable that blocks generation, or a fill-in prompt that names the missing fact (PM-002, PM-004). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PM-001 — Manifest diff.** Verifies: PM-001, PM-005, PM-010. Check (automated): generate a fresh project into a scratch directory and run `diff <(cd <output> && find . -type f | sort) <repo>/templates/mandated-manifest-<type>.txt` — the manifest shipped in this repository's `templates/` directory, never a locally reconstructed copy. Scope: this is a generation-time (step-0) check; files that later playbook steps mandate (for example performance-budget.json, PRIVACY_REGISTER.md, the CI workflow) are expected additions recorded in progress.md, and when the diff is re-run later they are matched against those step records — they are not diff violations. Pass: zero differences, or every difference matched by a not-applicable entry with a reason in the generation record. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-002 — Unreplaced-token and marker scan.** Verifies: PM-002, PM-003. Check (automated): `grep -rn '{{' <output>/` and `grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME' <output>/` — both must return nothing. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block shipment; fix the template or the variable set, never the output alone. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-003 — Lint parity on generated output.** Verifies: PM-011. Check (automated): run `markdownlint <output>/**/*.md` on the freshly generated tree, using the starter configuration shipped with the mandated set (`templates/.markdownlint.json`, emitted into every generated project as `./.markdownlint.json`; DECISIONS D-017) unless the project has recorded its own documentation configuration in its decision log. Where markdownlint is not available in the agent's environment, the fallback is a documented manual style check of the generated Markdown against that same rule set — heading hierarchy, list and table structure, link syntax — with the check and its result recorded in progress.md; the automated run remains required wherever the tool exists. Pass: exit 0, zero errors, before the first commit (under the fallback: a recorded manual check with zero findings). Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-004 — Exception register review.** Verifies: PM-001, PM-009. Check (manual): read the generation record for the new project; every absent mandated file has a stated reason, and every mandated-set change the template embodies has a decision-log entry that predates the template version. Pass: zero unexplained absences and zero unlogged set changes. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Full set, or a recorded reason — never a silent gap.
- Structure and prompts ship; facts never do.
- An empty section is honest; a filled-looking one may not be.
- Fix the template, regenerate — never patch the output.
- Conditional files fire on real triggers only.

## Checklist

- [ ] Manifest diff is clean, or every absence has a recorded reason (PM-001, G-PM-001).
- [ ] No template file contains an invented name, metric, testimonial, or date (PM-003).
- [ ] Token and marker scan returns zero hits on the generated output (G-PM-002).
- [ ] Conditional files match the project type's triggers; undefined triggers are recorded as gaps (PM-005).
- [ ] Public projects include CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SUPPORT, and GOVERNANCE (PM-010).
- [ ] markdownlint passes on the generated tree before the first commit — or, where the tool is absent, the manual style check against the starter configuration is recorded (PM-011, G-PM-003).
- [ ] Template version bumped and changelogged; mandated-set changes have a prior decision-log entry (PM-008, PM-009).
