# readme-writing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file ; https://sourcegraph.com/blog/documentation-as-code
- **Depends on:** project-templates
- **Feeds into:** documentation-writing, handover

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** creating a project README, replacing scaffold output at project start, or changing anything the README states — what the project is, its status, its version, or how to run it.
- **Do NOT use when:** writing the depth the README points to — tutorials, how-tos, and reference belong to documentation-writing; operating procedures belong to runbook-writing. The README is the front door and index, never the manual.

## Rules

1. **PM-041 — Fixed front-door order.** The README carries, in this order: project name, one line stating what it is, who it is for, current status with a date, the quickstart, and a link index into the doc set (ARCHITECTURE, runbook, CHANGELOG, DECISIONS). A section that fits none of these moves behind a link.
2. **PM-042 — No boilerplate survives.** Every line of generator or template output (framework welcome text, default badges, placeholder sections) is replaced with project content or deleted before the README first ships; "we will fill this in later" is not a shipped state.
3. **PM-043 — Quickstart executed verbatim.** Every quickstart command is run exactly as written, in order, in a clean checkout, before the README ships and after any change to it. A command that fails, or needs a step the README omits, is a README bug fixed in the README or the project — never explained away.
4. **PM-044 — Badges report real systems only.** A badge is present only if it is generated by a live system: CI status from the actual pipeline, version from the project's version source of truth, coverage from the actual test run. Hand-written or static shields claiming a state nobody measured are prohibited.
5. **PM-045 — Link, never duplicate.** Each mandated file is linked exactly once from the index; its content is never copied into the README. Every fact has one canonical home, and the README's copy of a fact is a link to that home.
6. **PM-046 — Every claim verified against the system.** Features, commands, flags, ports, and requirements named in the README are checked against the actual project before shipping. A feature that does not exist yet is labeled with its planned status and date, or omitted.
7. **PM-047 — Status is dated and current.** The status line carries an ISO 8601 date and is re-verified whenever the README changes; a stated version must equal the version source of truth (git tag or package version). An undated status is treated as stale.
8. **PM-048 — One-sitting length.** The README is short enough to read in one sitting; when a draft grows past what a new reader can scan in a few minutes, the overflow moves into the doc set and the README keeps the link.
9. **PM-049 — Shortest path to running.** The quickstart is the minimum sequence from clone to a running project, with prerequisites (runtime versions, required services, env files) listed before the first command — never discovered mid-sequence.
10. **PM-050 — README changes ride with the change.** Any change that alters what the README states (a renamed command, a new prerequisite, a status change) updates the README in the same change; a merged change that leaves the README wrong is incomplete.
11. **PM-051 — Every link resolves.** Relative links point at files that exist in the repo; external links are checked with the link checker. A link to a planned-but-absent file is removed until the file exists.
12. **PM-052 — Names match the record.** The project name, product names, and terminology are spelled exactly as in the project's fact sheet and word list, in the title, body, and badge URLs alike.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-021 — Scaffold README shipped.** Banned: publishing the generator's default README (framework welcome text, "getting started" boilerplate, sample badges) as the project's front door. Defeats: DET-CON-002. Instead: replace or delete every scaffold line at project start (PM-042); the first shipped README is written for this project. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-022 — Decorative badges.** Banned: static or hand-made badges asserting build status, coverage, or version that no live system produced. Defeats: DET-CON-012. Instead: wire the badge to the real pipeline's badge URL, or remove it until the system exists (PM-044). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-023 — Untested quickstart.** Banned: shipping quickstart commands that were written from memory and never executed in a clean checkout. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: run every command verbatim in a clean checkout and fix the mismatch at its source before shipping (PM-043). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-024 — Features that do not exist.** Banned: describing planned, imagined, or removed features in the README as current capability. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: verify each named feature against the running system (PM-046); label planned work as planned, with a date, or cut it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-025 — Fossil status line.** Banned: a status or version statement left standing after it stops being true ("currently in alpha", a version two releases old, a roadmap dated last year). Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: date the status, re-verify it on every README change, and match the version source of truth (PM-047). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-PM-021 — Quickstart execution.** Verifies: PM-043, PM-049. Check: automated — in a clean clone, run the project's `scripts/readme-quickstart-check.sh`, which extracts the fenced shell blocks under the README's quickstart heading and executes them in order. Pass: every command exits 0 and the final state is the running project. Fail: block shipment; fix the README or the project. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-022 — Boilerplate and marker scan.** Verifies: PM-042. Check: automated — `grep -niE 'create-react-app|create vite|this template provides|getting started with .* framework|TODO|FIXME|lorem|description here' README.md` plus a diff of the README's first heading against the scaffold default. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block shipment until each hit is replaced or deleted. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-023 — Link integrity.** Verifies: PM-045, PM-051. Check: automated — `lychee README.md` for all links, and a manifest check that each mandated file for the project type appears as a link target. Pass: zero broken links and every mandated file linked exactly once. Fail: block shipment. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-024 — Fresh-reader test.** Verifies: PM-041, PM-048. Check: manual — a reader who has never seen the project reads the README once and states what the project is, who it is for, its current status, and the exact steps to run it. Pass: all four answers correct from the README alone. Fail: rewrite the failing section and re-test. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Front door and index — never the manual.
- If a command is printed, it was run, verbatim, in a clean checkout.
- A badge is a report from a live system or it is deleted.
- Every fact lives in one file; the README holds the link.
- Undated status is stale status.

## Checklist

- [ ] Sections follow the PM-041 order: what, who, dated status, quickstart, link index.
- [ ] No scaffold or template text remains (G-PM-022 clean).
- [ ] Quickstart executed verbatim in a clean checkout, all exit 0 (G-PM-021).
- [ ] Every badge is generated by a real system; version matches the source of truth (PM-044, PM-047).
- [ ] Every mandated file linked exactly once; no content duplicated from them (G-PM-023).
- [ ] Every named feature, command, and requirement verified against the actual project (PM-046).
- [ ] Fresh-reader test passed and recorded (G-PM-024).

# runbook-writing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D10 Project & Memory (PM)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Sources:** PagerDuty, "What is a Runbook?" (Limoncelli's runbook sections) — https://www.pagerduty.com/resources/automation/learn/what-is-a-runbook/ ; PROJECT_ANATOMY.md Appendix A, runbook.md row (Google SRE practice)
- **Depends on:** documentation-writing
- **Feeds into:** postmortem-writing, handover, incident-response

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an incident class recurs, an alert fires, or a procedure (deploy rollback, failover, certificate renewal, data backfill) must be executable by whoever is on call — including someone who did not build the system, at 3 a.m., under pressure.
- **Do NOT use when:** the document explains how the system works (that is documentation-writing / explanation), records a past incident (postmortem-writing), or is a one-off task never expected to repeat. A runbook is a procedure to execute, not a narrative to read.

## Rules

1. **PM-061 — One runbook, one incident class.** Each runbook covers exactly one alert, symptom, or repeated procedure. Two failure modes in one file get two files, each named for its trigger.
2. **PM-062 — Fixed section order.** Every runbook carries, in order: service overview, trigger/symptom, prerequisites, numbered steps, escalation, verification. No section is omitted; an inapplicable section states why.
3. **PM-063 — Steps are actions with expected results.** Each step is one action — an exact command or a concrete UI action — followed by the output or state that confirms it worked. A step with no expected result is unfinished.
4. **PM-064 — Branch on difference.** Where a step's output can differ, the runbook states what to do in each case ("if the pod does not appear, go to step 9"). The executor never has to guess which branch reality took.
5. **PM-065 — Exact, runnable values.** Commands are copy-paste runnable against the real system: real hostnames, real service names, real flags. Placeholder tokens (`<host>`, `your-server`, `example.com`) never survive into a shipped runbook.
6. **PM-066 — Prerequisites up front.** Access required, where credentials live (the vault or system name — never the secret values), tools to install, and the dashboards to open are all listed before step 1, never discovered mid-incident.
7. **PM-067 — The alert links here.** Every alert this runbook serves links to the runbook file, and the runbook's trigger section names that alert or symptom verbatim, so the path from page to procedure is one click and unambiguous.
8. **PM-068 — Escalation names a role.** The escalation path names a role (e.g. "database on-call"), how to reach it, and the condition or time threshold that triggers escalation. A person's name may appear additionally, never instead.
9. **PM-069 — Verification closes the runbook.** The final step is an observable check that proves resolution — a health endpoint returning 200, the alert cleared, a real user action succeeding — not the absence of error messages.
10. **PM-070 — Same-change updates.** A runbook is updated in the same change as any incident that used it and exposed an error, and after any change to the procedure it describes. A runbook known to be wrong is fixed or withdrawn that day, not left for the next incident.
11. **PM-071 — Written for the stranger.** The runbook must be executable by a competent engineer who did not build the system and has never seen this incident. Every term, system, and "usual" step is spelled out or linked.
12. **PM-072 — Reference generic process, never copy it.** Incident-wide process (declare the incident, open the timeline, notify stakeholders) is linked to the one canonical process document, not pasted into each runbook where copies drift apart.

## BAN list

- **BAN-PM-031 — The filler step.** Banned: a step that gestures at the work instead of specifying it ("check the database and fix any issues"). Defeats: DET-CON-006. Instead: give the exact query, the healthy output range, and the action for each outcome (PM-063, PM-064). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-032 — Placeholder values shipped.** Banned: unreplaced template values in commands, hosts, or contacts (`<your-db-host>`, `TODO: add command`, `admin@example.com`). Defeats: DET-CON-003. Instead: ship the real hostname, or the exact command that retrieves it (PM-065). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-033 — Person-only escalation.** Banned: an escalation path that names only an individual ("call Dave") with no role, channel, or fallback. Defeats: DET-CON-005. Instead: escalate to the owning role via the paging tool, with the time threshold stated (PM-068). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-034 — The stale runbook.** Banned: shipping or keeping a runbook whose commands, hosts, or thresholds no longer match the system, past its `last_reviewed` date. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: re-verify against the live system and update `last_reviewed`, or withdraw the runbook (PM-070). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-PM-035 — Resolution declared without verification.** Banned: ending a runbook at the fix ("restart the service and close the ticket") with no step that proves the user-visible problem is gone. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: end with the observable verification check and its pass value (PM-069). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-PM-031 — Structure check.** Verifies: PM-061, PM-062, PM-063. Check: automated — script asserts each runbook file contains the six PM-062 section headings in order, and that every numbered step is followed by an "Expected:" line. Pass: all runbooks conform. Fail: block the change. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-032 — Placeholder scan.** Verifies: PM-065, PM-066. Check: automated — `grep -rnE '<[a-z-]+>|TODO|FIXME|example\.com|your-[a-z]+|localhost' runbooks/` returns no hits outside explicitly marked illustrative blocks. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block the change. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-033 — Freshness gate.** Verifies: PM-070. Check: automated — compare each runbook's `last_reviewed` front matter against the project's review window (a project policy parameter; default 90 days). Pass: every runbook is inside its window. Fail: block release until re-verified or withdrawn. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-034 — Link check.** Verifies: PM-066, PM-067. Check: automated — run lychee over the runbooks directory; every dashboard, tool, and alert link resolves. Pass: zero broken links. Fail: fix or remove the link before merge. Recorded in: progress.md.
- **G-PM-035 — Cold-run drill.** Verifies: PM-063, PM-064, PM-071. Check: manual — someone other than the author executes the runbook in a drill or tabletop exercise and completes it without asking the author a single question. Pass: completed unaided; every hesitation is filed as a runbook fix. Fail: revise and re-drill. Recorded in: progress.md.

## Recall anchors

- Steps are actions with expected results — never explanations.
- Prerequisites before step 1; nothing is discovered mid-incident.
- Escalate to a role, not a person.
- The runbook ends by proving the fix, not by performing it.
- If an incident exposed an error, the fix lands in the same change.

## Checklist

- [ ] Sections present in order: overview, trigger, prerequisites, steps, escalation, verification (G-PM-031).
- [ ] Every step has an exact command or action and an "Expected:" result (PM-063).
- [ ] Every step whose output can differ carries a branch (PM-064).
- [ ] Placeholder scan is clean: no `<tokens>`, TODOs, or example values (G-PM-032).
